title: dummy_cert already sets AKI from CA public key hash, not CA SKI
answers: How is AuthorityKeyIdentifier set on leaf certs?
Does mitmproxy leaf cert have SKI?
Where to change AKI in generated certs?
body:
- `mitmproxy/certs.py:dummy_cert` already added an AKI via `x509.AuthorityKeyIdentifier.from_issuer_public_key(cacert.public_key())` (SHA-1 of CA pubkey), under an RFC 5280 4.2.1.1 comment.
- That only equals the CA's SKI if the CA computed SKI the same way (mitmproxy's `create_ca` does; user-supplied CAs may not). Fix: `from_issuer_subject_key_identifier(ca_ski_ext.value)` with fallback to the hash form when the CA has no SKI.
- Do NOT add a leaf SKI equal to the CA's (SChannel issue 6494, code comment).
- Test: `test/mitmproxy/test_certs.py:TestDummyCert.test_with_ca` (uses `tstore.default_ca._cert`) can compare the leaf AKI `key_identifier` with the CA SKI `.digest`.
applies: Only for leaf certs from dummy_cert; create_ca sets SKI on the CA itself.
